worked_example.problem: A teacher types the marks {a}, {b} and {c} into a spreadsheet, which shows “Class average: {(a + b + c) / 3}”. Which is data and which is information?
steps: The marks on their own are raw facts: data.
“Class average: {(a + b + c) / 3}” has been processed and has meaning: information.
worked_example.answer: The marks are data; the average is information.

cards.idea: Users include end users, programmers, technicians and data entry clerks.
example: A programmer writes apps; a technician repairs computers.

cards.idea: Data are raw facts; information is processed data that has meaning.
example: “{a}, {b}, {c}” is data; “The hottest day was {b} °C” is information.

cards.idea: Good information is correct, complete, up to date and clear.
example: Last year’s timetable is not up to date.

right.text: It is correct and up to date.

wrong.explain: Old information may be out of date.
